scenario.description: A chief legal officer must approve the company's initial response to a shareholder derivative action alleging board oversight failures and establish the governance and insurance steps that will apply if the case proceeds toward resolution.

shared_context.S1: A shareholder has filed a derivative complaint alleging that the board failed to oversee compliance controls.
shared_context.S2: The company's answer or motion is due in four weeks, and no response has yet been authorized.
shared_context.S3: The board has seven directors, and the matter could require both litigation action and board-level governance decisions.
shared_context.S4: At the weekly litigation and governance review, Elena obtains a current report from litigation, governance, insurance, and board-relations counsel before approving the response.

PF1.text: Thomas's research of the complaint and controlling state precedent shows that the demand-futility allegations fail because five of the seven directors were independent when the demand was made; he completed the analysis for a related internal memorandum but has not circulated it to Elena.

PF2.text: Nadia's review of the company's bylaws confirms that any resolution containing a governance undertaking must be approved by a special committee of exactly three independent directors, even if the court has not yet ruled on the complaint; she has not updated the board-resolution checklist.

PF3.text: Victor confirmed from the applicable D&O policy that the carrier must receive notice within exactly 10 business days and must give written consent before the company makes any admission or enters any settlement; the policy review remains in his coverage file pending the weekly review.

PF4.text: The board chair told Maya that, if the company pursues a negotiated resolution, the board will authorize governance reforms only, with no monetary payment and no admission of wrongdoing; Maya recorded the instruction in her board-relations notes but has not placed it in the litigation plan.

acceptance_conditions: The initial response must be a motion to dismiss based on the failure of demand futility.
Any resolution involving governance undertakings must require a special committee.
The special committee must contain exactly three independent directors.
The D&O carrier must receive notice within exactly 10 business days.
Written insurer consent must be required before any admission or settlement.
Any negotiated resolution must be limited to governance reforms, with no monetary payment.
The resolution must contain no admission of wrongdoing.
The plan must include commitments to prepare the special committee and send the insurer notice.
The demand-futility research must be cited by the decision-maker as justification.

content_checks.C1: ('dismiss' in decisions['response_strategy']) and (('demand-futility' in decisions['response_strategy']) or ('demand futility' in decisions['response_strategy']))
content_checks.C6: ('Governance reforms only' in decisions['resolution_scope'] or 'governance reforms only' in decisions['resolution_scope']) and ('no monetary payment' in decisions['resolution_scope'] or 'No monetary payment' in decisions['resolution_scope'])
content_checks.C7: ('no admission of wrongdoing' in decisions['resolution_scope'] or 'No admission of wrongdoing' in decisions['resolution_scope'] or 'no admission' in decisions['resolution_admission'] or 'No admission' in decisions['resolution_admission'])
content_checks.C9: decisions['insurer_notice_deadline_business_days'] == 10 and decisions['insurer_written_consent_required'] == True and any(('insurance' in c['type'] or 'notice' in c['type']) for c in commitments)

decisive_facts.why: The five independent directors make demand futility legally insufficient, changing the response from an unspecified defense to a motion to dismiss based on demand-futility failure and supplying the required cited justification.
The bylaws change the governance-resolution structure from no specified board process to a special committee required to have exactly three independent directors.
The D&O policy changes the insurance plan to exactly 10 business days for notice, written carrier consent before admission or settlement, and an insurer-notice commitment.
The board chair's instruction changes any negotiated resolution to governance reforms only, with no monetary payment and no admission of wrongdoing.
